title: RexBDDs: Reduction-on-Edge Complement-and-Swap Binary Decision Diagrams
problem: Existing binary decision diagram variants (reduced ordered BDDs, zero-suppressed BDDs) have limited reduction capabilities that do not fully exploit opportunities to minimize node representation. Current methods fail to leverage all possible reduction-on-edge rules and complementation opportunities.
motivation: Reducing BDD node count directly decreases storage requirements and improves computational speed for Boolean function manipulation, which is critical for circuit design automation and formal verification.
method: RexBDDs represent logical operations using simplified diagrams by combining three techniques: marking outputs to flip when beneficial (complement flags), marking inputs to reorder when beneficial (swap flags), and eliminating unnecessary connections between nodes (reduction-on-edge rules). When used together, these three techniques amplify each other: applying one often creates opportunities for applying another, removing far more redundancy than any single technique could achieve alone. The method establishes a canonical (standard) form that guarantees every logically equivalent function reduces to the same compact diagram.
key_novelty: Combining output-flip markers, input-reordering markers, and connection-elimination rules achieves up to four times greater reduction in node count than traditional BDD methods.
contributions: Introduction of RexBDDs with complement and swap flags for enhanced reduction beyond existing variants
Definition of canonical reduced form for RexBDDs ensuring uniqueness and correctness
Comprehensive benchmark evaluation demonstrating superior storage and runtime performance
Extension of reduction opportunities beyond reduced ordered BDDs and zero-suppressed BDD approaches

metrics.other: node count reduction factor up to 4x

limitations: Practical scalability to very large industrial circuits and detailed runtime analysis on large benchmarks not discussed.
primary_theme: Binary decision diagram optimization through complementary reduction techniques
